transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-18 15:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Walker (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Samira Gomez (CSM), Jordan Li (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Chen (Dir IT, Sequoia), Carlos Ruiz (Security Eng), Lena Park (PM), Tom O'Neill (Infra)

Summary (auto):
Quick POC scoping to confirm security/compliance gating for pilot, workload sizing, benchmark goals, and timeline. Customer requires SOC2/ISO artifacts, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC/audit logs, and optional customer-managed KMS. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics
- Security & compliance checklist (SOC2, ISO, SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS)
- Pilot success criteria (latency, accuracy, throughput, data handling)
- Workload sizing and bench plan
- Timeline and provisioning needs

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan: alright everyone, thanks for joining, uh we wanted to kick off, um the scoping for the Sequoia security pilot, I think we have about an hour, hi Maya, hi Carlos, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Dr. Maya: thanks Ethan, yes we have a bunch of questions around, you know, compliance requirements and how Redwood will be handling PHI during the pilot, so want to be sure we're aligned.
[00:28] Priya: absolutely, we expected that — we'll walk through SOC 2/ISO artifacts, SSO options, RBAC and audit logs. Also want to understand your workload so we can size a Dedicated pool for bench runs.
[00:43] Carlos: quick note — Sequoia's baseline is SOC 2 Type II plus ISO27001, and we need evidence. Also SSO via SAML with SCIM provisioning and role mappings.
[00:54] Ethan: totally, we'll send the SOC 2 report and ISO cert, and our SAML docs. For pilot we often provide a staging Dedicated environment with VPC peering or Private deployment if necessary.
[01:10] Tom: VPC peering is preferred, on-prem might be overkill for the pilot, but security ops will want to see audit trails and immutable logs.
[01:20] Jordan: logs are captured at token/request level in our console with exportable audit trail, we also keep admin activity logs — that can be shipped to your SIEM via secure syslog or S3 with encryption.
[01:31] Carlos: is that supported for both Hosted and Dedicated? we need guaranteed retention and tamper evidence.
[01:38] Priya: yes, Dedicated and Private have longer retention and you can configure a dedicated audit log sink. For tamper evidence we support append-only S3 buckets with MFA delete per your policy, and we can provide signed log digests.
[01:54] Dr. Maya: KMS — do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) for data at rest? We need keys controlled by our KMS.
[02:03] Ethan: yes, for Private and Dedicated we can integrate with customer KMS/HSM, and for Hosted we offer bring-your-own-key in certain regions — we'll include the KMS integration matrix in the docs.
[02:18] Lena: on success criteria, product wants <300ms p95 for interactive queries, and an accuracy bar on our eval set — around 92% intent accuracy. Also zero data egress from the pilot tenant.
[02:31] Priya: that's reasonable. For p95 latency we need to understand average input length and concurrency — can you share typical tokens per request and expected peak RPS?
[02:42] Tom: rough numbers: avg 120 tokens per request, peak 40 RPS during clinic hours, sustained 10 RPS off-peak. Burst to 120 RPS possible for batch imports.
[02:55] Priya: thanks — that maps to a small Dedicated pool with 4 GPUs for throughput benching; we'll size and propose. For latency benching we'll run p95 and p99 tests with your sample prompts.
[03:07] Ethan: for the benchmark harness we'll push a repo with scripts to run avgs, tail latency, memory/kv cache effects, and we'll also include quantization variants to test cost/latency tradeoffs.
[03:21] Dr. Maya: what about model variants? we need a fallback in case of capacity or higher latency.
[03:27] Jordan: we support routing policies and can fallback to smaller quantized variants; defaults can be configured per-route during pilot.
[03:35] Carlos: regarding RBAC — we need role-based admin separation, least privilege, and SSO group mappings to Redwood roles, plus audit for role changes.
[03:46] Priya: yes, we support RBAC with fine-grained roles and SAML/SCIM group sync. We'll show the role matrix and example policies.
[03:55] Lena: are there any known gaps in Redwood's compliance posture for healthcare customers? PHI specifically?
[04:02] Ethan: we don't take a position on PHI by default, but our Private deployments and Dedicated with VPC & CMK are the recommended path. We'll share our security doc that outlines controls and recommended architecture for PHI.
[04:16] Carlos: do you do penetration tests or provide pentest reports?
[04:21] Samira: yes we do annual penetration tests and can provide redacted executive summaries; for enterprise customers we have enhanced options.
[04:28] Tom: timeline — how quickly can we spin up a trial environment and run the first bench?
[04:34] Priya: typical timeline: 1) share artifacts and access (SOC2, ISO) within 48 hours; 2) provision Dedicated staging in 3-5 business days; 3) run bench and initial eval over 2 weeks; so roughly 3 weeks to get initial results.
[04:50] Ethan: given we want to sync to your procurement window, does that timeline fit?
[04:54] Lena: yes procurement is aiming for decision end of Q2, so a March pilot aligns.
[05:02] Ethan: ok great. Let's capture success criteria explicitly — is this OK: p95 latency < 300ms, accuracy on eval set >= 92%, no external data egress, audit logs enabled and retained 12 months, SSO with SAML/SCIM, CMK for keys if required.
[05:18] Dr. Maya: yes, add requirement for signed audit digests and SIEM export.
[05:24] Carlos: add RBAC mapping and admin separation. Also escalation path for incidents during pilot.
[05:31] Priya: we'll add incident reporting SLA for the pilot (e.g., 4 hour initial response) and include that in the pilot agreement.
[05:40] Ethan: any blockers we haven't covered?
[05:42] Tom: need to validate network — VPC peering and IP allowlist, plus any egress restrictions. We'll share firewall and peering contacts.
[05:50] Jordan: we also will provide a Runbook with step-by-step for peering, SAML setup, and test harness execution.
[05:58] Lena: on evaluation we'll have product and clinical champions run a set of 250 sample queries and a holdback set for regression checks.
[06:07] Priya: perfect, we'll coordinate the eval harness and create a spreadsheet for telemetry (latency, tokens, accuracy, confidence scores).
[06:16] Ethan: ok let's recap next steps...
[06:20] Recap (multiple voices):
- Redwood to email SOC2/ISO certs and security portal link (Ethan)
- Redwood SE to provision bench repo and staging Dedicated environment (Priya)
- Customer to send sample PII-free eval set and workload KPIs (Tom/Lena)
- Customer secops to confirm KMS and retention requirements (Carlos)
- Schedule security deep-dive next week (Samira to propose times)

[06:45] Dr. Maya: thanks everyone, this is helpful, look forward to the docs and the bench results.
[06:49] Ethan: thanks all, we'll follow up by EOD with the artifacts.

Note: transcript contains occasional mis-attributions and subtle transcription errors (e.g., "KV cash" instead of "KV cache", some proper nouns slightly off). References: security portal https://redwood.ai/security, bench repo link will be shared in follow-up.
